title: Tight Quantum Collision-Resistance Bounds for Multi-Round Sponges
summary: The first nontrivial collision-resistance bound for multi-round sponges is non-tight; determining a tight quantum-query bound with optimal parameter dependence remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine tight collision-resistance bounds for sponge constructions with more than one round against quantum algorithms that make $q$ quantum queries to a uniformly random permutation $\pi$ on $\{0,1\}^{r+c}$ and its inverse. The first nontrivial collision-resistance bound for this multi-round setting is known, but it is non-tight. The unresolved task is to obtain a tight bound, including tight dependence on the quantum-query budget and the sponge and round parameters.

scope.domain: Quantum collision resistance of multi-round sponge constructions in the random-permutation model.
assumptions: The permutation is uniformly random, with quantum query access to it and its inverse.
parameters: r and c: sponge parameters whose sum determines the permutation input length
Number of rounds: the sponge round parameter, restricted to more than one round
scope.unresolved_remainder: Obtain a tight collision-resistance bound with tight dependence on the quantum-query budget and the sponge and round parameters.

citations.label: Quantum Lifting for Invertible Permutations and Ideal Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents the first nontrivial collision-resistance bound for sponges with more than one round and explicitly states that it is non-tight. A tight multi-round bound remains open.
citation_labels: Alexandru Cojocaru et al., Quantum Lifting for Invertible Permutations and Ideal Ciphers
